In order to free the rules in a chain via call_rcu
to stash a rcu_head and space for a pointer at the end of the rule array.
When the current nft_rule_dp blob format got added in
2c865a8a28a1 (""netfilter: nf_tables: add rule blob layout"")
in a double-trailer:
size (unsigned long)
struct nft_rule_dp
struct nft_expr
struct nft_rule_dp
struct nft_expr
struct nft_rule_dp (is_last=1) // Trailer
The trailer
column3: is not accounted for in size

column1: so it can be located via start_addr + size.
Because the rcu_head is stored after 'start+size' as well this means the
is_last trailer is *aliased* to the rcu_head (struct nft_rules_old).
This is harmless
column2: because at this time the nft_do_chain function never

column1: evaluates/accesses the trailer
column2: it only checks the address boundary:

column1: for (; rule < last_rule; rule = nft_rule_next(rule)) {
But this way the last_rule address has to be stashed in the jump
structure to restore it after returning from a chain.
nft_do_chain stack usage has become way too big
column2: so put it on a diet.

column1: Without this patch is impossible to use
for (; !rule->is_last; rule = nft_rule_next(rule)) {
... because on free
column2: the needed update of the rcu_head will clobber the

column1: nft_rule_dp is_last bit.
Furthermore
column2: also stash the chain pointer in the trailer

column1: to recover the original chain structure from nf_tables_trace infra
without a need to place them in the jump struct.
After this patch it is trivial to diet the jump stack structure
done in the next two patches.
